questions.question: Which domain separation support level includes the ability for service providers to create or modify processes per customer?

explanation.correct: At the Standard support level, business logic allows the service provider (SP) to create or modify processes per customer. The use cases reflect proper use of the application by multiple SP customers in a single instance.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Basic level ensures data goes into the proper domain but does not specifically enable per-customer process customization
Enhanced level adds tenant-configurable business logic, but Standard is where SP process customization begins
Advanced is not a defined domain separation support level

source.excerpt: Standard - Business logic: The service provider (SP) creates or modifies processes per customer. The use cases reflect proper use of the application by multiple SP customers in a single instance.

questions.question: Which business logic and processes can be domain separated by the instance owner in Security Incident Response? (Choose three)

options.text: Email parsing rules for incident creation

explanation.correct: Business logic and processes that can be domain separated by instance owner include: Email parsing rules for incident creation, Security incident SLAs, Workflows for incident response orchestration, as well as user groups, integrations, business rules, risk score calculators, escalation paths, and process definitions.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Platform user authentication methods are not domain-separated; they are global platform configurations
Database connection strings are infrastructure-level configurations, not domain-separated business logic

source.excerpt: Business logic and processes that can be domain separated by instance owner: Email parsing rules for incident creation, Workflows for incident response orchestration, Security incident SLAs

questions.question: In a domain-separated Event Management environment, which statement is true about MID Server configuration?

options.text: A single MID Server can serve all domains simultaneously
Each MID Server can serve only one domain according to the integration user it uses
MID Servers are not affected by domain separation
Multiple MID Servers must share the same service account

explanation.correct: In a multi-domain environment, each MID Server can serve only one domain according to the integration user that it uses. In the configuration of the connector instance, you must make sure that the MID Server uses the same domain as the Connector instance.

wrongAnswers.explanation: MID Servers are domain-specific based on their integration user; they cannot serve all domains
MID Servers are affected by domain separation through their integration user configuration
Different domains require different service accounts/integration users for their MID Servers

source.excerpt: In a multi-domain environment, each MID Server can serve only one domain according to the integration user that it uses. In the configuration of the connector instance, make sure that the MID Server uses the same domain as the Connector instance.

questions.question: What is NOT fully supported when implementing domain separation in GRC applications?

explanation.correct: While GRC supports separation of data, separation of logic and process is not fully supported. Many types of records in GRC are automatically generated through user processes, and the domain of automatically generated records is the same as the domain of the user creating them.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data separation is fully supported in GRC domain separation
UI separation is part of the runtime domain separation support
Reporting separation is supported through domain separation at runtime

source.excerpt: While GRC supports separation of data, separation of logic and process is not fully supported.

questions.question: A tenant domain owner wants to manage their own Security Incident Response operations. Which capability can they configure independently within their domain?

explanation.correct: Tenant domain owners can create their own incident response workflows, incident categories, incident response knowledge base articles, and runbooks to be associated with incident response workflows. This enables domain-specific process customization.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Platform system properties are typically global and not domain-separable
Global authentication settings are platform-wide, not domain-specific
Database schema modifications are platform-level changes, not tenant-configurable

source.excerpt: Tenant domain owners can create their own incident response workflows. Tenant domain owners can create their own incident categories, incident response knowledge base articles, and runbooks to be associated with incident response workflows.

questions.question:
Evaluate the following statements about domain separation and CMDB reconciliation rules:

Statement 1: Identification rules used during the identification process are always defined at the global level.

Statement 2: Reconciliation definition rules can be defined for different domains.

Which statements are TRUE?

explanation.correct: Both statements are TRUE. The identification rules and identification inclusion rules used during the identification process are always defined at the global level - tables like Identifier (cmdb_identifier) do not have a sys_domain field. The reconciliation definition rules that are used during the reconciliation process can be defined for different domains - tables like Reconciliation Definition (cmdb_reconciliation_definition) do have sys_domain field.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both statements are true; reconciliation rules can be domain-specific
Both statements are true; identification rules are indeed global
Both statements are true as documented in the IRE domain separation guide

source.excerpt: The identification rules and identification inclusion rules used during the identification process are always defined at the global level. The reconciliation definition rules that are used during the reconciliation process can be defined for different domains.

questions.question: Which elements can be domain-separated in a service provider use case? (Choose four)

explanation.correct: In a service provider use case, client scripts, business rules, workflows, and processes can be domain-separated. This allows different tenants to have customized business logic while sharing the same instance.

wrongAnswers.explanation: System dictionary entries (sys_dictionary) are platform tables that should NOT be domain separated as it can produce unexpected results
Platform update sets are deployment mechanisms, not domain-separated business logic

source.excerpt: In this use case, client scripts, business rules, workflows, processes, and so on can be domain-separated.

questions.question: Starting with which ServiceNow release can third-party integrations in Security Incident Response be configured and activated on a per-domain basis?

explanation.correct: In the Madrid release, third-party integrations can be configured and activated on a per-domain basis. This means that the integration activated and configured in one domain cannot be leveraged in another domain, allowing for domain-specific integration configurations.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Kingston had integrations under single domain, not per-domain configuration
London allowed integrations across multiple domains but not per-domain configuration
New York continued the Madrid functionality; Madrid was the release that introduced per-domain integration configuration

source.excerpt: Madrid - All integrations can now reside across multiple domains. In the Madrid release, third-party integrations can be configured and activated on a per-domain basis.

questions.question: In a domain-separated Event Management environment, alert groups are created based on which criteria?

options.text: Alerts from all domains are grouped together
Alert groups are created only for alerts in the same domain
Alert groups are based on CI type, ignoring domains
Alert groups are manually assigned by administrators

explanation.correct: Alert Aggregation is supported in domain-separated environments, and alert groups are created only for alerts in the same domain. This ensures that alerts from different tenants are not incorrectly aggregated together.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Alerts from different domains are NOT grouped together; domain separation is enforced
Domain is a critical criterion for alert grouping; CI type alone does not override domain separation
Alert groups are created automatically based on domain and aggregation rules, not manually assigned

source.excerpt: Alert Aggregation - Supported. In domain-separated environments, alert groups are created only for alerts in the same domain.

questions.question: At the Enhanced support level for domain separation, what additional capability is provided compared to Standard support?

options.text: Service provider can create processes per customer
Tenants can modify business logic for themselves based on defined use cases

explanation.correct: At the Enhanced support level, data-driven process enables service provider customers (tenants) to modify business logic that is based on defined use cases. These configurations are UI-based and fail-safe so that configurations by one customer cannot affect another.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Basic data separation is provided at the Basic support level, not Enhanced
Service provider creating processes per customer is the Standard support level capability
Runtime UI separation is part of Basic support level

source.excerpt: Enhanced - Data-driven process enables service provider customers to modify business logic that is based on defined use cases. These configurations are UI-based and fail-safe so that configurations by one customer cannot affect another.

questions.question:
Evaluate the following statements about domain separation in Performance Analytics:

Statement 1: In the Global approach, Performance Analytics records like indicators and breakdowns are all in the global domain.

Statement 2: In the Domain-specific approach, each domain must have users with pa_admin role for managing Performance Analytics.

Which statements are TRUE?

explanation.correct: Both statements are TRUE. In the Global approach, Performance Analytics records such as indicators and breakdowns are all in the global domain, and data collection jobs respect the domains of facts table records. In the Domain-specific approach, the Performance Analytics records themselves are domain-separated, and each domain has users with pa_admin and other roles for managing Performance Analytics.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both statements are true; Domain-specific approach does require pa_admin users per domain
Both statements are true; Global approach does keep PA records in global domain
Both statements are true as documented in PA domain separation approaches

source.excerpt: Global: The Performance Analytics records, such as indicators and breakdowns, are all in the global domain. Domain-specific: The Performance Analytics records themselves are domain-separated. Each domain has users with pa_admin and other roles for managing Performance Analytics.

questions.question: A Security Incident Response capability like Sighting Search is invoked in a domain-separated environment. How are domain-specific implementations handled?

options.text: Only global integrations are used regardless of domain
The capability invokes a domain-specific implementation based on the security incident's domain
Users must manually select which integration to use
Capabilities are disabled in domain-separated environments

explanation.correct: Capabilities that are invoked stay generic across domains with domain-specific implementation of the capability being called. For example, a Sighting Search on an IP can invoke a Splunk implementation in one domain and a QRadar implementation in another.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Starting with Madrid, integrations can be domain-specific, not just global
The capability automatically uses the domain-specific implementation without manual selection
Capabilities are fully supported in domain-separated environments with domain-specific implementations

source.excerpt: Capabilities that are invoked stay generic across domains with domain-specific implementation of the capability being called. For example, a Sighting Search on an IP can invoke a Splunk implementation in one domain and a QRadar implementation in another.

questions.question: Which three approaches to domain separation are available in Performance Analytics? (Choose three)

explanation.correct: There are three approaches to domain separation in Performance Analytics: Global (PA records in global domain, respects fact table domains), Domain-specific (PA records themselves are domain-separated with pa_admin per domain), and Hybrid (low-level records global, high-level records domain-separated).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Federated is not a defined PA domain separation approach
Distributed is not a defined PA domain separation approach

source.excerpt: There are three approaches to domain separation in Performance Analytics: Global, Domain-specific, Hybrid.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true about orchestration workflows in a domain-separated Security Incident Response environment?

options.text: Workflows created in one domain aren't visible in another domain
Workflows for incident response can be customized per domain
Workflows automatically sync across all domains
Tenant domain owners can create their own incident response workflows

explanation.correct: Orchestration workflows created in one domain aren't visible in another domain - they do NOT automatically sync across all domains. Each domain maintains its own set of workflows, and tenant domain owners can create their own incident response workflows independently.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This statement is TRUE; workflows are domain-isolated
This statement is TRUE; workflows can be customized per domain
This statement is TRUE; tenants can create their own workflows

source.excerpt: Orchestration workflows created in one domain aren't visible in another domain. Tenant domain owners can create their own incident response workflows.

questions.question: When editing alert management rules in a domain-separated Event Management environment, what restriction applies to workflow selection?

options.text: Any workflow from the instance can be selected
Only global workflows can be selected
Users can only apply relevant workflows visible in their domain
Workflows must be approved by a global administrator

explanation.correct: Remediation is supported in domain-separated Event Management. While editing alert management rules, users can only apply relevant workflows that are visible in their domain. This follows the principle of domain separation in Flow Designer.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Users cannot select workflows from domains they don't have visibility into
Both global and domain-specific workflows can be selected if visible to the user
There is no global administrator approval requirement for workflow selection; it's based on domain visibility

source.excerpt: Remediation - Supported. While editing alert management rules, users can only apply relevant workflows.

questions.question: Which SIR automation capabilities are configured in the domain of the security incident for response automation? (Choose three)

explanation.correct: Capabilities configured in the domain of the security incident for response automation include: Threat Lookup, Enrich Observable, Enrich Configuration item, Get Running Process, Get Network Statistics, Block Request, Isolate Host, Sighting Search, Email Search and Delete, and Publish to Watchlist.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Platform authentication is a global platform capability, not a domain-specific SIR automation capability
Instance upgrade scheduling is platform administration, not an SIR automation capability

source.excerpt: Capabilities are configured in the domain of the security incident for response automation. These capabilities include: Threat Lookup, Sighting Search, Email Search and Delete...
